before.title: Feeding mechanism
before.description: Risso’s dolphins primarily take squid and other cephalopods. The sparse anterior mandibular teeth, usually two to seven pairs with no upper teeth, differ from a dolphin’s full conical tooth rows. Some studied adults initiated deep foraging dives with a right-sided roll.
before.modelCoverage: Biological account. The closed-mouth exterior does not simulate prey capture or internal oral mechanics.

before.title: Respiration
before.description: A single dorsal blowhole admits air at the surface. Breathing is separate from feeding; submerged apnea does not use gills. The displayed slit is closed. Ventilation, oxygen stores and circulation are not computed.

before.title: Locomotion and control
before.description: Horizontal flukes are driven by dorsoventral bending of the posterior body. The source-derived exterior retains stable pectoral surfaces. The turn combines bank and heading change; flow, thrust, speed and energy use are not computed.
before.modelCoverage: Exterior kinematics, with no solved fluid forces or speed estimate.
